To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the RPM features are a powerful tool to deal with the PDE identification problem and that combining RPMs and gradient based algorithms is a promising approach to estimate accurate physical parameters of a heat exchangers.

(1) the RPMs can be used to estimate the parameters of the PDEs describing the heat exchanger; (2) the RPMs are a good initialisation for gradient based nonlinear optimisation algorithms; (3) the proposed approach is able to estimate the physical parameters of the heat exchangers.

the RPMs are a very interesting tool in the identification of PDEs, and that a two step identification procedure based on the RPMs and a gradient based optimisation is an effective way to identify a grey box model for a heat exchanger.

the combination of least squares and gradient descent based algorithms can be a powerful tool to deal with the challenging problem of identifying a co current flow exchanger.
